profile.name: Salman Rashid
profile.kicker: Macroeconomics · Monetary Policy · Applied Econometrics · Policy Analysis
positioning: I am an economist and policy researcher with a background in macroeconomics, monetary policy, and international relations theory. My work uses econometric methods, principally VAR and VECM modeling in Stata and EViews, alongside structured qualitative methods, including codebook thematic analysis and AI-assisted research workflows, to study how monetary policy moves through Pakistan’s economy and how the institutions that set it explain their own reasoning.

My current research centers on monetary policy transmission and central bank communication, extending toward industrial heterogeneity, and, over time, toward the wider technological, geopolitical, and maritime forces that shape how economic policy is made and how its consequences unfold across the economy.
profile.openTo: Research-oriented roles in economic consulting, central banking, international organizations, and think tanks, and exploring PhD opportunities in Economics. Open to remote, onsite, and hybrid work, worldwide.

eag.title: Associate Member, Economic Advisory Group (EAG)
eag.summary: A year-long mentored research programme focused on macroeconomic and policy research, with responsibility for developing four policy briefs.
eag.firstBrief: The first policy brief, Diagnosing Inflation: The SBP Monetary Policy Committee’s Causal Narratives and Their Empirical Fit (2022–2026), has been completed and presented to the EAG Committee. Revisions were requested, including condensing the document to 2,000–3,000 words.
eag.work: Contributing research, evidence synthesis, and analytical inputs to policy-oriented discussions within the programme.

researchInterests.title: Macroeconomics & Monetary Policy
researchInterests.description: Building on my work in monetary transmission, structural breaks, inflation dynamics, and central-bank communication, I am developing an interest in modern macroeconomic modelling, including New Keynesian DSGE frameworks, open-economy and financial-friction models, and heterogeneous-agent approaches such as TANK and HANK. I am particularly interested in using these frameworks to study monetary transmission, distributional effects, and the interaction between monetary policy and real economic behaviour.

researchInterests.title: AI, Technology & Labour
researchInterests.description: The economic effects of artificial intelligence on productivity, employment, labour demand, research practices, and economic decision-making, with particular interest in AI adoption and the changing economics of knowledge work.

researchInterests.title: Political Economy & Geoeconomics
researchInterests.description: How institutions, incentives, social cohesion, state capacity, external shocks, and international economic forces shape economic behaviour, policy, and development.

researchInterests.title: Maritime Economics & Conflict
researchInterests.description: How geopolitical conflict and disruption affect trade routes, shipping, exchange rates, imported inputs, production costs, and macroeconomic stability.

researchProjects.summary: Empirical research on monetary policy transmission to Pakistan’s manufacturing sector using a structural break-adjusted VECM, with exchange-rate, interest-rate, and credit channels examined together.

researchProjects.title: Diagnosing Inflation: The SBP Monetary Policy Committee’s Causal Narratives and Their Empirical Fit (2022–2026)
researchProjects.meta: Economic Advisory Group · Presented to the EAG Committee
researchProjects.summary: A codebook thematic analysis of 36 SBP Monetary Policy Statements examining how the Committee explains inflation, which causes it emphasises or downplays, and how stated diagnoses compare with subsequent inflation dynamics.

researchProjects.title: A Theoretical and Empirical Account of Heterogeneous Monetary Transmission across Pakistan’s Large-Scale Manufacturing Industries
researchProjects.shortTitle: Heterogeneous Monetary Transmission across Pakistan’s Manufacturing Industries
researchProjects.meta: Salman Rashid · Industry-level VECM estimation in progress
researchProjects.summary: A theoretical and empirical study of why manufacturing industries respond differently to common monetary and macroeconomic shocks, using observable industry characteristics and a common VECM framework.
